speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and exactly when these symptoms began?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, or decreased fetal movement? Also, have you experienced any diarrhea or nausea since the symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever. I also have Headache, Anorexia, Fatigue, Malaise. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis seems inconsistent with acute fever and headache, especially given your recent ice cream consumption. I need to rule out Listeria monocytogenes infection, so I will request specific tests and imaging. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, CBC, Listeria_Serology REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Cultures: Gram-positive rods that are catalase-positive and show distinctive tumbling motility in the liquid medium. Complete Blood Count: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, Platelets 200,000 /μL.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood culture results showing Gram-positive rods with tumbling motility are classic for Listeria monocytogenes, confirming my suspicion of listeriosis. Given your pregnancy and the confirmed pathogen, I will proceed with treatment to protect both you and the fetus. DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis
